subject: general
question: Joint forest management is an example of which of the following?
solution:
Joint Forest Management (JFM) is a collaborative approach to forest management that involves local communities and government forest departments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It is based on the principle that local communities have a vested interest in the sustainable management of their forests, and that they should be given a say in how their forests are managed.
 
• JFM is an example of a **participatory approach** to development.
 
• Participatory approaches emphasize the importance of involving local communities in the planning and implementation of development projects.
 
• This can lead to more sustainable and effective development outcomes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• Single-man dominance is an example of a top-down approach, in which decisions are made by a single individual or small group of individuals.
 
• Economic equality is an example of a distributive justice approach, which focuses on the fair distribution of resources.
 
• Political equality is an example of a procedural justice approach, which focuses on ensuring that everyone has a fair opportunity to participate in decision-making processes.

Hence, Joint forest management is an example of** participatory approach.**
